In HackerRank, the duration a test remains active is determined by the expiration settings configured for that specific test or invitation. By default, the expiry option is set to 'Never', meaning invitations do not expire unless manually configured.

### Key Points

- **Custom Expiration:** You can define a specific start and end time (including time zone) to control the active window for a test.
- **Default Behavior:** If no specific expiration is set, the invitation remains active indefinitely.
- **Post-Expiration:** Once a test expires, invited candidates can no longer access the test, the 'Invite' button is disabled, and you cannot invite new candidates.

2. Locate the **Expiry** dropdown menu.
3. Review the current setting or select **Custom** to define a specific date, time, and time zone.
4. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

detailed_results.predicted_response:
### Overview

In HackerRank, test variants are designed to streamline your assessment process when evaluating candidates across different tech stacks (e.g., Node.js, Python, or Java) within a single test setup. 

### When to Use Test Variants

Use variants when you want to assess candidates for the same role but allow them to choose or be assigned a specific technology or stack. This approach allows you to maintain a single, streamlined test configuration rather than managing multiple separate tests.

### Advantages of Test Variants

- **Reduced Maintenance:** Manage one test setup instead of multiple individual tests.
- **Personalized Experience:** Candidates only see sections relevant to their chosen stack.
- **Clean Reporting:** Reports are specific to the variant attempted, ensuring insights remain role-specific and easy to evaluate.
- **Improved Candidate Experience:** Candidates receive helpful subtext for each variant, allowing them to make informed decisions before starting.

### When to Create a New Test

Create a new, separate test when you are assessing for distinct job roles, different experience levels, or unique skill sets that do not share a common core assessment structure. You can build these from scratch or use HackerRank's recommended questions based on the specific role requirements.

### Reference

- [Test Variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/3121307537-july-2025-release-notes)
- [Create Test Variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/7530103378)
- [Creating a New Test](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/6967597139-creating-a-new-test)

Overview

You can accommodate a candidate's request for extra time by modifying their test duration directly in your HackerRank for Work account. If you need to send a new invitation, you can do so separately.

Steps to Add Extra Time

1. Log in to your HackerRank for Work account.
2. Go to the Tests tab and select the relevant test.
3. Navigate to the Candidates tab.
4. Select the checkbox next to the candidate.
5. Click More > Add Time.
6. Enter the additional time in minutes (e.g., 53) and click Confirm.

Note: If the candidate is currently in a session, they must refresh their page to see the updated timer. If they have already submitted the test, you may need to re-invite them.

Steps to Re-invite a Candidate

1. Go to the Tests tab and open the specific test.
2. Navigate to the Candidates tab.
3. Select the checkbox next to the candidate.
4. Click Invite selected.
5. In the Send Test Invites section, click Send invite.
6. When prompted, click Re-invite to send the invitation again.

2. Go to the **Candidates** tab.

3. Select a candidate profile.

 1. Verify that the correct **Job** is selected.

Call Visa India at 000-800-100-1219 to report a lost card. 

From anywhere else in the world, Visa's Global Customer Assistance Service is reachable 24/7 at +1 303 967 1090 and can block your card within ~30 minutes of being reported, plus arrange emergency cash and a replacement card
detailed_results.predicted_response:
### Reporting a Lost or Stolen Visa Card

If your Visa card has been lost or stolen, you should take immediate action to secure your account.

#### Steps to Report
1. Visit the official Visa India [Lost or Stolen card page](https://www.visa.co.in/support/consumer/lost-stolen-card.html).
2. Follow the instructions provided to report and block your card.
3. If you require emergency services, such as an emergency card replacement, this can also be requested through the same portal.

#### Additional Support
For further assistance, you may contact Visa Global Customer Assistance Services (GCAS). It is recommended to keep a record of your card account number and the relevant GCAS telephone number for your region in a secure location.

Reference: https://www.visa.co.in/support.html

FAQ

### What should I do if my Visa card has been lost or stolen?

To report your Lost or Stolen Visa Card, please visit our [Lost or Stolen card](/support/consumer/lost-stolen-card.html) page. Our skilled support team can assist you at any time with reporting and blocking your Lost or Stolen card and look into providing you emergency services* if applicable.

### How can I find an ATM?

To find an ATM, please use Visa’s [ATM locator](https://www.visa.com/atmlocator/) to get currency at over 2 million ATMs worldwide.

### Security

### I was contacted by someone claiming to be from Visa. Is this real or a scam?

If you receive a call or email asking for your information, do not provide it. You can report a phone scam that uses Visa’s name by [contacting us](/contact-us.html). Visa does not call or email cardholders and request personal information.

### My identity has been stolen – what should I do?

Visit our [Lost or Stolen card](/support/consumer/lost-stolen-card.html) page – if the identity theft involves your Visa card – to learn how to cancel your card or get an emergency replacement card.

### Travel

### What do I need to know before I travel abroad?

Travel tips for every stage of your journey

### Get in touch with your bank

Check that your bank or credit card company has updated contact information. Tell them where and when you’ll be travelling – so that your card isn’t flagged for unusual activity.

### Know the emergency numbers for lost or stolen cards

Take note of your card account number and the telephone number for the Visa Global Customer Assistance Services (GCAS) of the country you are travelling to. Visa cardholders can report lost or stolen Visa cards and request emergency services by calling the GCAS number. Learn more about GCAS here.

Get support

Need help? Give us a call For lost or stolen credit cards, please call us:

Travel tips for every stage of your journey

### Activate your credit and debit cards before you travel

Check with your bank to confirm that your payment card has been activated for overseas travel use and take note of the daily ATM withdrawal limit for your card. Know the expiry dates, account balance and amount of credit available to you. This way, you won’t be caught short with a card that doesn’t work while you’re away, or not have enough credit to cover your trip expenses.

### Apply for mobile alerts

Sign up for free SMS transaction alerts to receive instant SMS messages when a transaction exceeds a pre-set amount or when unusual card activities are detected.

### Memorise your PIN

Whether you are using a magnetic strip or chip card, know your credit card PIN before travelling overseas. If you have forgotten your PIN, reapply for a new one.

### Make a copy of everything in your wallet

Keep a record of card account numbers and telephone numbers for reporting lost or stolen cards. But remember to keep this information in a safe place. Always keep your credit card number and the three-digit CVV2 code on the back of your Visa card confidential.

### Get in touch with your bank

File an inquiry

### Report an in-store purchase issue

Use this online form to report a problem you had when trying to use your Visa card.

[Report a purchase issue](https://usa.visa.com/Forms/visa-rules.html)

### Inquire on a Visa rule

Make an inquiry regarding the Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules.

[File a Visa rule inquiry](https://globalclient.visa.com/rule-inquiry)
